subtype: Eye contact norms with elders in India [Mismatch]
passage:
“Sonali, why do you look down when Nanaji talks to you?” asked Saurabh, who had just moved to Delhi from Manchester.
“It's respect. Looking straight at elders can seem rude.”
“At my old school, looking down would mean you were hiding something.”
“That's silly! I'm not hiding anything.”
“I know, I know. I just think it's different.”
Nanaji laughed from his chair. “Both my grandchildren are honest, whichever way they look.”
Sonali looked up at him and smiled. Saurabh grinned.

qa.q: Where had Saurabh just moved from?
qa.a: He had just moved to Delhi from Manchester.

qa.q: What might Sonali have felt when Saurabh said looking down would mean hiding something?
qa.a: A bit offended and defensive, since she called it silly, though she then listened when he said it is just different. She may also have wondered how others read her.

qa.q: How could the cousins avoid misunderstanding each other?
qa.a: By asking what each way of looking means to the other, and remembering that neither lowered eyes nor steady eye contact proves honesty or disrespect.

qa.q: How does Nanaji see the two children's eyes?
qa.a: He judges them as honest whichever way they look, so he does not treat the eyes as proof.

grounding: Lowered eyes with elders can show respect while steady eye contact can signal honesty elsewhere; neither is proof.

subtype: Eye contact norms with elders in India [Mismatch]
passage: I'm Sunaina. In my old school in Pune, I looked down when teachers spoke, to show respect. Now in Toronto, Mr Vikas said, “Please look at me so I know you're listening.” I tried, and my eyes felt hot and strange. At recess I told him that where I come from, looking down is polite. He said, “Thanks for telling me. I didn't know. I'll remember that you're listening even when you look down.” Now I look up sometimes and sometimes I don't, and it is fine either way.

qa.q: Which city did Sunaina move to?
How did Sunaina feel when Mr Vikas asked her to look at him, and what else might explain his request?
qa.a: Uncomfortable, since her eyes felt hot and strange. Mr Vikas probably wanted a sign she was listening, not to be unkind.

qa.q: What worked well in how Sunaina handled it?
qa.a: She told him calmly what lowered eyes mean where she comes from, and that gave him what he needed to understand her.

qa.q: How might Mr Vikas have first read Sunaina's lowered eyes?
qa.a: Perhaps as not listening or being shy. He asked for eye contact to check, and later changed when she explained.

grounding: Eye contact norms differ between families and schools; neither shows honesty or disrespect.
